findings.title: Blocked-email checks can be bypassed by changing email case
findings.body: The lookup compares the submitted value directly against `blocked_emails.email` without canonicalizing it. Email local/domain case variants (for example, a block entry for `user@example.com` and a signup using `USER@example.com`) will not match on the case-sensitive database column, allowing a blocked address to register. This is especially problematic because other user-email paths use `Email.downcase`, so the application already treats emails as canonicalized for lookup purposes. Normalize both blocked-email storage and lookup (and enforce a matching normalized unique index) before querying.

findings.title: Match counters lose updates under concurrent signup attempts
findings.body: `should_block?` reads a row, increments `match_count` in memory, and saves it back. Concurrent validations can read the same count and each write the same incremented value, so some blocked-email attempts are silently omitted from the statistics. Use an atomic database update such as `update_all("match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?", ...)`, or lock the row, so the tracking fields remain accurate under concurrent requests.
